At the podium on Tuesday, Anthony Weaver compared Aeneas Peebles to Kyle Williams, who spent 13 outstanding seasons with the #Bills.

Williams lists now at 6'1", 303 and played 1/3 tech where he was undersized but posted 48.5 career sacks, made 6 Pro Bowls, and was once AP2.  He averaged 681 snaps per season, which is iron-man level by today's standards.

Incredibly, Williams has yet to be included in the Bills Wall of Fame (their RoH equivalent), but that is almost certainly coming soon, since he retired in 2018.

Kelly Gregg had nothing like the same pass rush productivity (20.5 career sacks, less pressures/QHs), but in terms of tenure, position, relative size, and fan reverence he'd be a comp for Williams.

As this relates to Fub, I think Weaver is picking a traits comp that is a stretch goal for on-field production.  I scored Peebles for 6 pressure contributions on Sat vs the Vikings, including 2 that helped close the exits on sacks.  My notes from the Vikings game are attached.

He's been one of the Ravens big risers this camp and I can't see why the Ravens would leave him off the roster after the Summer he has had.

I think the OLB5 race is very close indeed.

Any of the 3 OLB5 candidates currently on the roster would play a ST "Big" role on the OL for punt team.  Individually:

Rucker has played well, and has 3.5 years of team control (0.5 terminology for RFA season) but may be a player the #Ravens may believe they can keep on the practice squad with minimal poaching risk.

Burke has shown pass rush juice, screen awareness, and has additional value on the FGBLK team where he could move into a role previously held by Brent Urban.  However, the Ravens don't need another "kick inside" guy for passing downs with Young and Robinson on the roster.  He has some poaching risk if cut (probably less than 30% for a waiver claim, but he might have offeres and decide to sign with a different practice squad)

Isaac has shown the most as a pass rusher in 11x11 work since he has returned, but he's had 2 years of injury issues and is under contract only through the 2027 season.

I think it's still possible the Ravens don't love their pass rush depth and go outside for a vet, where they have had success over the last 5-6 seasons (Clowney, Houston, Pierre-Paul, Ngakoue, Van Noy).  EDC has used that as a formula to get solid results with limited dollars and production-based incentives.  One downside to this group is that none would be expected to play ST.

The Ravens may also want someone with coverage skills to add pass rush flexibility.  Van Noy might be the best candidate from that perspective.
